body.x: Engineers developing 5G, Wi-Fi 7 and microwave components rely on vector network analyzers (VNAs) to measure how signals behave across wide frequency ranges. In Korea, that market has long been led by established brands, and buyers in high-precision testing tend to be cautious about switching to an instrument they have not used themselves.
Could a newer analyzer earn that trust simply by letting engineers test it on the spot?

iTest Korea, the official Korea Global Service Center and branch of RF and wireless communication test equipment maker iTest, is taking that approach at KES 2026. Led by CEO Sangjoon Park, the company is exhibiting at the show and running live demonstrations of its VNA4265 at the booth, along with one-on-one consulting sessions with application engineers.

The VNA4265 is a benchtop VNA covering 100 kHz to 26.5 GHz, designed for RF and microwave component testing. According to the company, it offers a 135 dB dynamic range, trace noise below 0.002 dB RMS and integrated time-domain analysis functions based on time-domain reflectometry (TDR). iTest Korea also supplies wireless connectivity testers and, beyond hardware, provides technical support, calibration, application consulting and user training for customers in Korea.

iTest, founded in 2011, says it supplies test equipment to Qualcomm, MediaTek, Realtek, Huawei, ASUS and Hikvision, and that its VNAs and wireless connectivity testers are used in R&D centers and manufacturing lines in the United States, Europe, Japan, Taiwan and Singapore. The group operates across China, where it is headquartered, as well as Korea, Taiwan, the United States, Europe and Southeast Asia.

iTest Korea names low brand awareness among Korean engineers as its main hurdle. Starting with KES 2026, it plans to add hands-on demonstrations of the VNA4265, offer evaluation units and provide rapid technical support and tailored consulting to Korean customers. It also aims to work with iTest's network in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific to grow its share of next-generation wireless testing, including 5G, 6G and Wi-Fi 7.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
